explanation: The histone H4K5 acetyltransferase activity (GO:0043995) is enabled_by AT2G45160, which is SCARECROW-LIKE 27 (UniProtKB:Q7XJM8). SCL27 is a GRAS transcription regulator that also carries the alias HAM1 (HAIRY MERISTEM 1). The acetyltransferase in all three cited papers (PMID:17877703, PMID:23273925, PMID:25183522) is the MYST protein HAM1, AT5G64610 (UniProtKB:Q9FLF7; UniProt gene names HAM1 HAG4 At5g64610). The enabler should be AT5G64610. HAM2 (AT5G09740) is redundant and could be added.

explanation: The MRG2 H3K36me3 reader activity has AT2G45160 (SCL27, a GRAS protein with the alias HAM1) as a has_input. The partner the paper reports is the MYST acetyltransferase HAM1, AT5G64610 (UniProtKB:Q9FLF7). Separately, a recruited effector enzyme is not the input of a reader activity. The MRG2-to-HAM1 relationship is already captured by the causal edge to the acetyltransferase activity, so the has_input should be removed rather than re-pointed.

explanation: This 1998 ISS row (no With/From) gives CBL4/SOS3 (O81223, AT5G24270) calcium-dependent protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity on the basis of its similarity to the calcineurin B regulatory subunit, made when SOS3 was cloned (PMID:9632394). In fungi and animals the phosphatase activity belongs to the catalytic calcineurin A subunit, not to calcineurin B, so the transfer does not hold even for a true calcineurin B ortholog. Plants have no calcineurin A homolog, no phosphatase partner of SOS3 has been found, and SOS3 instead binds and activates the SOS2 (CIPK24) protein kinase. We suggest withdrawing the row.

Instead, SOS3 was found to interact with and activate a protein kinase encoded by SOS2."}, {"reference_id": "PMID:10725350", "supporting_text": "no genes similar to CNA have been identified from plants, yet"}]

explanation: This 1998 ISS row (no With/From) places CBL4/SOS3 (O81223, AT5G24270) in the calcineurin complex, on the cloning-time hypothesis that SOS3 acts through a calcineurin-like phosphatase (PMID:9632394). The calcineurin complex is the calcineurin A/B phosphatase heterodimer; plants have no calcineurin A, and the SOS3 effector identified since is the SOS2 (CIPK24) kinase, with which SOS3 forms a kinase complex. We suggest withdrawing the row.
supported_by: [{"reference_id": "PMID:10725350", "supporting_text": "Our results imply that plant salt tolerance may be mediated not by a calcineurin-like protein phosphatase but, rather, by the SOS3/SOS2 kinase complex."}]

explanation: This IMP row annotates CBL4/SOS3 (O81223, AT5G24270) to GO:0042539 hypotonic salinity response, defined as a response to a decrease in salt concentration. The cited paper (Liu and Zhu 1997) isolates sos3 as a mutant hypersensitive to Na+ and Li+ stress and assays growth inhibition on added NaCl, i.e. a response to an increase in salt concentration. The term should be GO:0042538 hyperosmotic salinity response; the qualifier and evidence can stay as they are.

explanation: PMID:21631432 reports heterocyclic-ligand binding "uniquely" for GSTF2 and GSTF3. In the phi-GST nomenclature, GSTF3 is At2g02930 (Q9SLM6). This annotation is instead on GSTF6 (At1g02930, P42760), whose only link to the name is the legacy alias "AtGSTF3". QuickGO returns this paper's binding IDAs for GSTF2 (P46422) and GSTF6 but none for Q9SLM6, the pattern expected from mapping the paper's "GSTF3" through the alias. We could not read the full text. Please check it: if GSTF3 was assayed, move the annotation to Q9SLM6; if only GSTF2 bound the ligand, delete this row. The abstract names GSTF3 only for the heterocyclics and attributes camalexin and quercetin-3-O-rhamnoside binding to GSTF2, so deletion is the more likely outcome for this ligand.

explanation: This 2003 TAIR row asserts DNA binding for SERRATE (Q9ZVD0, AT2G27100), which the evidence does not support. Biochemical work shows that the SE N-terminal and zinc-finger regions bind RNA and DCL1, and SE associates with chromatin through RNA polymerase II complexes rather than by binding DNA itself. The row is ISS, citing the SE cloning paper (PMID:11402159), but has no With/From entry naming a characterized homolog; the cloning paper only noted a single C2H2-type zinc finger and speculated about chromatin modification, which is not a sequence-similarity transfer. We suggest withdrawing the row.

explanation: This 2003 TAIR row asserts DNA-binding transcription factor activity for SERRATE (Q9ZVD0, AT2G27100), but SE belongs to the ARS2 family of RNA effector proteins, whose characterized members act in RNA processing, not as sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factors. The row is ISS with no With/From entry, so no characterized homolog is named, and the cited reference (Riechmann et al. 2000) is a genome-wide census of Arabidopsis transcription-factor families; SE was presumably counted because of its single C2H2-type zinc finger. No valid ISS source for this activity exists. We suggest deleting the row (or, if TAIR wishes to keep it, supplying the With/From homolog so it can be assessed).

explanation: This IPI row makes SERRATE (Q9ZVD0, AT2G27100) part_of the nuclear cap binding complex because it binds both CBC subunits, CBP20 (AT5G44200) and CBP80/ABH1 (AT2G13540) (PMID:24137006). The nuclear cap binding complex is the CBP20/CBP80 heterodimer; SE is an associated partner, as ARS2 is in the metazoan CBC-ARS2 assembly, not a subunit. The IPI evidence fits the molecular function mRNA cap binding complex binding (GO:0140262), with the qualifier changed from part_of to enables; human SRRT/ARS2 carries that term.
